name: esphome
summary: Firmware and device configuration framework for ESP32 and ESP8266 based IoT hardware.
why_it_matters: ESPHome captures useful IoT device capability knowledge, but current Vrooli usage does not justify claiming supported end-to-end firmware and hardware workflows.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs custom sensor or actuator firmware on ESP devices.
Operators want YAML-driven embedded device configuration instead of custom firmware development.
The workflow needs local device management tied to home automation or telemetry scenarios.

platform_support.notes: The build tooling is broadly portable, but flashing, serial access, and device support depend heavily on host hardware and drivers.

prerequisites: Configuration and secret handling model for device firmware
implementation_notes: Promotion should define device lifecycle ownership from config generation through flashing.
Future support should prioritize a small number of validated board types.
operational_notes: Hardware access is the main portability constraint.
OTA updates and secret rotation need deliberate handling.
Validation should prove a real compile and device deployment path.
risks: Hardware-dependent tooling is easy to overstate as cross-platform.
A generic wrapper would not guarantee that any real board workflow works.
